text: A risk register and an FMECA (failure modes, effects and criticality analysis) exist for this element and are current.
guidance: Keep both under revision control and reference the revision in the evidence entry. Applies from TRL 4 upwards.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: The NREL Marine Energy Technology Development Risk Management Framework requires a risk register and an FMECA from TRL 4 upwards for WPTO open-water projects.

text: The relevant-environment test used conductive seawater (or a documented, justified equivalent) wherever electrical coupling, galvanic effects or corrosion are plausible.
guidance: If the element cannot be exposed to seawater (for example, a dry-cabinet subsystem), mark the criterion N/A and justify it.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: Ocean-specific coupling paths — conductivity, galvanic corrosion, biofouling-driven leakage — do not appear in air-only or fresh-water tests, so an air-only test does not demonstrate the relevant environment for a marine deployment.

text: Environmental extremes representative of the deployment were tested (temperature and cold soak, humidity inside the enclosure, immersion or pressure) and the conditions were recorded with the results.
guidance: Applies from TRL 5 through TRL 6. Record the actual measured conditions, not the specification.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: Arctic and open-ocean deployments expose equipment to cold, condensation inside enclosures and hydrostatic pressure; a test whose conditions were not recorded cannot be shown to be relevant.

text: A pre-deployment test plan exists that distinguishes deck or dockside results from open-water results.
guidance: Name which results were obtained alongside or on deck and which were obtained at sea.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: Deck and dockside conditions can misrepresent at-sea performance, especially for communications, motion response and grounding, so results from the two settings must not be pooled.

text: Field duration and failure events are logged, with a root-cause status recorded for each failure.
guidance: Applies from TRL 6 through TRL 7. A failure without a root-cause status counts as open.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: Claiming that engineering feasibility is fully demonstrated requires knowing how long the element ran and why it stopped; an unexplained failure leaves the demonstration unproven.

text: Critical functions of the prototype use production-intended parts; any hand-built critical part is covered by a documented build specification.
guidance: List the critical parts and state, for each, whether it is production-intended or hand-built.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: The EERE TRL 7 definition requires a near-production-quality prototype; a hand-built critical part without a build specification cannot be reproduced and so is not near-production-quality.

text: The calibration procedure and the data path are documented, and transmitted values have been shown to match the calibrated values.
guidance: Applies from TRL 7 through TRL 8. Include the comparison between the raw, calibrated and transmitted values for at least one deployment.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: For observing-system use the number that reaches the user is the product; an undocumented data path can silently alter calibrated values.

text: A data submission pathway to the intended observing programme is established and has been exercised (where the technology feeds an observing programme).
guidance: Mark N/A with a justification if the technology does not feed an observing programme.
mandatoryBasis: Tailored requirement of this framework; see rationale.
rationale: For ocean-observing technologies the end-user specification includes delivery into the observing system, so a device that cannot submit data has not demonstrated the end-user specification.
